profile.name: Mahfujur Rahman Joy
profile.bio: Civil & Environmental Engineer working as a **Research Consultant at CEGIS**, a public trust under the Ministry of Water Resources, Bangladesh, while pursuing an **M.Sc. in Water Resources Development (WRD) at BUET**. I build river models, read the Earth from orbit, and use machine learning to understand floods and droughts in a changing climate.

tools.name: GapLens
tools.tagline: Find, fill & compare gaps in hydroclimate records
tools.description: Load a streamflow, water-level, rainfall or groundwater record with its neighbours and GapLens maps the gaps, recommends methods, ranks 70+ filling methods by hiding real observations and scoring how well each one restores them, and fills the record. Includes a rating-curve editor with automatic segments and year-by-year curves. Real Python (Pyodide) running in your browser.
features: 70+ methods: interpolation, seasonal, regression, neighbour stations, ML, state-space
Hold-out comparison: NSE, KGE, RMSE over a ladder of gap lengths
Recommends methods from the gap pattern and the data at hand
Rating curves: live editor, automatic breaks (BIC), year-by-year curves
Reads Excel and BWDB files: title rows, REGULAR rows, daily means
Python in the browser: about 40 MB on first start, then cached

tools.name: Series Generator
tools.tagline: Fill gaps and extend hydrological records
tools.description: Learns the seasonal pattern, spread and day-to-day memory of a series, then fills the missing values or adds plausible years before or after the record. Includes an accuracy test for the filled values.
features: Gap filling: model, random, linear or seasonal
Extend by years: statistical model or resampled years
Built-in accuracy test for filled holes
Multi-sheet workbooks, plots and Excel export

tools.name: Min-Max-Avg Terminal
tools.tagline: Daily, monthly & yearly statistics from any time series
tools.description: Load a water-level, discharge or rainfall record and get the minimum, maximum and average for every day, month and year — with an interactive range chart, a sortable table and Excel export.
features: Reads .xlsx, .csv, .txt or rows pasted from Excel
Finds the date and value columns automatically
Min–max band chart with hover values
Export results to .xlsx

tools.name: Dependability Analyzer
tools.tagline: Dependable water level, flow & rainfall for reports
tools.description: Rank a long record with the Weibull plotting position (or Gringorten, Cunnane, Hazen) and read off dependable low and high values at any P. Filter years and months, convert the datum (e.g. mPWD to mMSL), and export report-style figures, a dependability table, a methods paragraph and an Excel workbook.
features: Dependable low and high values at any P
One value per year or every value, whole series or by month
Year and month filters, incomplete-year warnings
Datum conversion, e.g. mPWD to mMSL
Reads BWDB files: title rows, REGULAR rows, daily mean of readings
Report-style figures (PNG), dependability table, Excel and report text

tools.name: Hydro ML Studio
tools.tagline: Machine learning for water level, discharge & rainfall
tools.description: Train and compare eight machine-learning models to simulate or forecast a hydrological series: automatic lag, rolling and seasonal features, cross-validation, Grid / Random / Bayesian tuning, NSE · KGE · PBIAS with Moriasi ratings, gap filling and Excel export.
features: SVR, random forest, extra trees, gradient boosting, neural network, KNN, tree, Lasso
Save & reload trained models
One-click zip of all results & plots
n-fold time-series cross-validation
Grid, random & Bayesian hyper-parameter tuning
Importance, partial dependence, duration curves
Recursive gap filling & prediction on new files
Methods paragraph + full Excel report

tools.name: DSBC Studio
tools.tagline: Downscaling & bias correction of climate data
tools.description: Statistical downscaling and bias correction of daily, weekly or monthly climate series. Screen predictors with partial informational correlation, train and honestly validate 11 regression models, then correct climate-model runs with 10 univariate and 5 multivariate methods, checking that each correction keeps the model's projected change. Real Python (Pyodide) running in your browser.
features: Predictor screening: correlation, mutual information, stepwise PIC
11 downscaling models with grid, random or Bayesian tuning
Blocked-year cross-validation, scored against the seasonal cycle
QM, QDM, SDM, CDF-t, NBC and more, calibrated on the past only
Multivariate: MRNBC, MBCp, MBCr, MBCn, R2D2
Checks that the projected climate change is kept
